prunlgp: installation and user guide

Source: PRUNLGP.md

prunlgp() selects internal inputs in a linked Gaussian process emulator using validation performance. It refits the receiving component after removing an input and recomputes predictions through the network. Each component has one output; different receivers can retain different inputs from the same source.

This guide takes you from installation to a working example, HTML tutorials and automated tests. The fork’s prunlgp-master branch contains the complete implementation, based on upstream dgpsi-R master. The R package is named dgpsi; prunlgp is a function within it.

  • Function reference
  • Synthetic tutorial
  • Operational-data tutorial
  • Recorded versions and results

Follow sections 1–4 in order for your first example. Sections 5–6 cover tutorial rendering and tests from a local clone. Commands labelled R belong in the R console or an R script; commands labelled Terminal belong in a shell.

1. Requirements

Item Requirement and purpose
R The package declares R >= 4.0; this contribution was tested with R 4.4.2.
Python Use Python 3.10 for the tested setup. The upstream initializer also supports 3.11 and 3.12. You can let init_py() install Python in its Conda environment.
Conda Miniconda, Miniforge or Anaconda; init_py() offers to install Miniconda when no Conda executable is found.
Git Needed to clone the repository and install the Python development backend. Make git available on your system PATH.
R build tools If dependencies need compilation, use Rtools matching your R version on Windows, Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, or the required compiler/system libraries on Linux.
Pandoc Required for tutorial HTML. It is bundled with RStudio; otherwise install it separately and make it available to R Markdown.
Internet Required for the initial R and Python dependency installation.

The fork installs its R imports, including reticulate, ggplot2 and visNetwork. The commands below also install the tutorial and test tools. init_py() manages the Python dependencies, including NumPy, SciPy, Numba, scikit-learn, FAISS and the Python dgpsi package. A separate system Python installation is not needed for this route.

2. Install the complete fork

R — start in a fresh session:

install.packages(c("remotes", "rmarkdown", "knitr", "htmlwidgets", "testthat"))
remotes::install_github(
  "zhuangchaoqun/dgpsi-R", ref="prunlgp-master",
  dependencies=NA, upgrade="never", build_vignettes=FALSE
)

Restart R after installation, especially if another dgpsi version was loaded. Then check the installed package:

library(dgpsi)
stopifnot("prunlgp" %in% getNamespaceExports("dgpsi"))
find.package("dgpsi")
packageDescription("dgpsi")[c("Version", "RemoteUsername", "RemoteRef", "RemoteSha")]

The export check must complete without an error. For a GitHub installation, the remote should identify zhuangchaoqun and prunlgp-master. A version label alone does not distinguish this fork from other development installations.

Install the full branch rather than sourcing R/prunlgp.R alone. The function uses registered methods and helpers, including support for networks with no internal links and restoration of saved linked models. build_vignettes=FALSE keeps installation separate from model training; section 5 executes the tutorials.

3. Set up Python once

R — run interactively before starting any terminal scripts:

library(dgpsi)
init_py(py_ver="3.10", dgpsi_ver="dev")
set_thread_num(1)
reticulate::py_config()
reticulate::py_run_string("import dgpsi; print(dgpsi.__file__)")

Accept the installation prompts if the required environment is missing. If the initializer requests an R restart, restart and run these commands again. py_config() should show the intended Python interpreter, and importing dgpsi should print its module location without an exception. The current initializer uses the Conda environment dgp_si_R_2_6_0_dev for this explicit dev setting.

The R branch and Python backend are separate choices. This fork is based on R master; the verified tutorials use the Python dgpsi development backend. Keep dgpsi_ver="dev" consistent in the example, tutorial runner and tests. Calling init_py() with different settings may select a different environment. See the upstream initializer documentation.

The published results used Python 3.10.20 and backend commit 480bb30260d3a1c22af1ddffe1a11df3e4de0820. Installing a later dev revision may change numerical results. Record your environment when comparing runs; see section 8 for the recorded-backend option.

4. Complete example with the supplied data

Run the following R blocks in order in the same session. This example needs only the installed fork, not a local source clone. It uses the operational sample; the main tutorial instead generates synthetic data.

4.1 Load the package and data

library(dgpsi)
init_py(py_ver="3.10", dgpsi_ver="dev")
set_thread_num(1)

data_file <- system.file("extdata", "prunlgp_example.csv", package="dgpsi")
stopifnot(nzchar(data_file))
dat <- read.csv(data_file)
train <- subset(dat, split == "train")
validation <- subset(dat, split == "validation")
test <- subset(dat, split == "test")
global <- paste0("x", 1:16)
outputs <- c("a", "b", "c")
stopifnot(nrow(train) == 96L, nrow(validation) == 48L, nrow(test) == 96L)
table(dat$split)

The supplied measurements are de-identified and already centred and scaled using training rows only. x1–x16 are available global inputs; u and v are intermediate outputs; a, b and c are the outputs scored during pruning. Observed u and v train the component models. At validation and test time, the network receives only global inputs and predicts its internal variables.

4.2 Train one DGP per output

features <- list(
  u=c("x1", "x2", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10"),
  v=c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x11", "x12"),
  a=c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v"),
  b=c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v"),
  c=c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v")
)

# Match the original fitting seeds to the group seeds used by prunlgp.
component_seed <- function(id) as.integer((57 + 104729 *
  match(id, sort(names(features)))) %% 2147483646 + 1)

components <- lapply(names(features), function(id) {
  set_seed(component_seed(id))
  dgp(as.matrix(train[, features[[id]]]), as.matrix(train[, id, drop=FALSE]),
      id=id, name="sexp", depth=2, node=2, N=40, B=20, ess_burn=10,
      share=FALSE, bounds=c(0.1, 10), prior="ga", nugget_est=TRUE, verb=FALSE)
})

The five scalar models use the same architecture and fitting budget. In the initial network, each of a, b and c receives both u and v.

4.3 Build the initial linked network

connections <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(features), function(id) {
  f <- features[[id]]
  internal <- f %in% c("u", "v")
  data.frame(
    From_Emulator=ifelse(internal, f, "Global"),
    To_Emulator=id,
    From_Output=ifelse(internal, 1L, match(f, global)),
    To_Input=seq_along(f)
  )
}))
stopifnot(sum(connections$From_Emulator != "Global") == 6L)
network <- lgp(connections, components, B=20, verb=FALSE)

From_Output selects a global matrix column or a source model’s output. To_Input is the column position in the receiving model’s training matrix. The six internal connections are u and v to each of a, b and c.

4.4 Prune using validation predictions

refit <- function(model, keep, seed) {
  dgpsi::set_seed(seed)
  dgpsi::dgp(model$data$X[, keep, drop=FALSE], model$data$Y,
      id=model$id, name="sexp", depth=2, node=2, N=40, B=20, ess_burn=10,
      share=FALSE, bounds=c(0.1, 10), prior="ga", nugget_est=TRUE, verb=FALSE)
}

selected <- prunlgp(
  network, components,
  x=as.matrix(validation[, global]),
  y=lapply(validation[, outputs], as.numeric),
  refit=refit, seed=57, B=20, protect=0,
  search="subsets", max_rounds=2, max_evals=32, verb=TRUE
)
print(selected)
selected$history[, c("evaluation", "stage", "loss", "internal_links",
                     "admissible", "selected")]

The objective is the mean validation RMSE normalised by each scored output’s training standard deviation. protect=0 additionally rejects any candidate that increases a scored output’s validation RMSE beyond numerical tolerance. keep refers to columns of the original training matrix, and refit uses training data only. Test responses do not enter selection.

search="subsets" visits each receiving model and evaluates its internal-input subsets. For a larger network, search="backward" evaluates individual deletions. The initial network remains eligible. The function returns the best admissible evaluated graph; a run can correctly retain all links when no evaluated deletion improves the selection criterion.

4.5 Predict and inspect held-out errors

set_seed(57)
before <- predict(selected$initial_model, as.matrix(test[, global]),
                  full_layer=TRUE)$results
set_seed(57)
after <- predict(selected, as.matrix(test[, global]), full_layer=TRUE)$results

# Flatten the layer lists while retaining emulator IDs.
means <- function(result) do.call(c, unname(result$mean))
errors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(outputs, function(id) {
  data.frame(
    output=id,
    validation_unpruned=unname(selected$initial_rmse[id]),
    validation_pruned=unname(selected$rmse[id]),
    test_unpruned=sqrt(mean((as.numeric(means(before)[[id]])-test[[id]])^2)),
    test_pruned=sqrt(mean((as.numeric(means(after)[[id]])-test[[id]])^2))
  )
}))
print(errors, row.names=FALSE)

stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(errors[, -1]))),
  selected$score <= selected$initial_score + selected$settings$tolerance,
  all(selected$rmse <= selected$initial_rmse + selected$settings$tolerance))

Use selected$initial_model for the comparison: it has the same imputation settings as the selection procedure. The per-output protection applies to validation errors. The test table reports performance on the held-out sample, where an improvement is not guaranteed.

4.6 View and save the actual networks

print(summary(selected$initial_model))
print(summary(selected))
subset(selected$structure, From_Emulator != "Global")

output_dir <- file.path("tutorial-output", "quick-start")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(summary(selected$initial_model),
  file.path(output_dir, "initial-network.html"), selfcontained=FALSE)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(summary(selected),
  file.path(output_dir, "pruned-network.html"), selfcontained=FALSE)
write.csv(errors, file.path(output_dir, "errors.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
cat("Quick-start example completed.\n")

The interactive networks appear in the RStudio Viewer. Outside RStudio, open the saved HTML files in a browser. Keep their accompanying asset directories when copying them. The output folder is relative to getwd().

A successful example prints the completion message, creates both HTML files and a finite error table, and passes the validation checks above. Removing an input from one receiving model does not remove it from other receivers.

5. Run the tutorials and regenerate HTML

The installed package supplies the data and functions. To run the supplied rendering scripts or tests, also obtain the source repository.

Terminal — clone once:

git clone --branch prunlgp-master https://github.com/zhuangchaoqun/dgpsi-R.git
cd dgpsi-R

If you downloaded a GitHub ZIP instead, select prunlgp-master, extract it and open that directory. Subsequent relative paths assume the repository root, which contains DESCRIPTION, tools, vignettes and tests.

Terminal — execute and render both tutorials:

Rscript tools/run-prunlgp-tutorial.R
Rscript tools/run-prunlgp-tutorial.R prunlgp-operational

The first command generates the synthetic example. The second uses the supplied operational CSV. Each command fits new models, performs pruning and renders the HTML; it does not reuse saved model results. Python must already be set up interactively as in section 3.

From RStudio, the main tutorial can also be run with source("tools/run-prunlgp-tutorial.R") from the repository root. To render either article directly in R:

Sys.setenv(DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_VIGNETTE="true", DGPSI_TUTORIAL_BACKEND="dev")
rmarkdown::render(
  "vignettes/prunlgp.Rmd", output_dir="tutorial-output",
  knit_root_dir=getwd(), envir=new.env(parent=globalenv())
)
# For the companion, use vignettes/prunlgp-operational.Rmd and
# output_dir="tutorial-output/operational".

The runner is recommended because it also checks results and saves numeric tables. A direct render() call creates the article but does not export those additional CSV/RDS files. The explicit DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_VIGNETTE=true flag enables computations; without it, the vignette code is displayed but not run.

Runner output Synthetic tutorial Operational tutorial
Output directory tutorial-output/ tutorial-output/operational/
HTML file prunlgp.html prunlgp-operational.html
Numeric records errors.csv, system-errors.csv, intervals.csv Same file names in its directory
Search and structure search.csv, structure.csv, connections.csv Same file names in its directory
Run information session-info.txt, results.rds Same file names in its directory

Success ends with Tutorial completed in ... seconds., an HTML path and no R error. The runner checks three scored outputs, six initial internal links, finite errors and the objective/per-output validation protection. Inspect search.csv for failed or rejected candidates; a failed candidate is recorded even when the overall run succeeds. Re-running writes to the same output folder, so copy it elsewhere first if you want to retain an earlier run.

To rebuild the complete local pkgdown website, including navigation and both executed articles, run from the repository root:

install.packages("pkgdown")
Rscript tools/build-prunlgp-site.R

Open docs/index.html afterwards. This is a local build; it does not publish anything to GitHub. It takes longer because it rebuilds package documentation and runs both tutorials. The prunlgp reference and tutorials retain their page-specific author credits; other pages use the upstream package credits. The fork’s published site is deployed from gh-pages after this executed build has been checked. The inherited upstream website workflow does not run on prunlgp-master; use the executed build above when publishing this extension. The commands below run the package and native tests locally.

6. Run automated tests

Start a fresh R session in the source repository root, using the installed fork. The complete native test suite needs the Python environment from section 3.

library(dgpsi)
stopifnot("prunlgp" %in% getNamespaceExports("dgpsi"))
Sys.setenv(DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_TESTS="true", DGPSI_TEST_BACKEND="dev")
test_results <- testthat::test_dir(
  "tests/testthat", filter="prunlgp", reporter="progress",
  stop_on_failure=TRUE, stop_on_warning=TRUE
)
test_table <- as.data.frame(test_results)
stopifnot(!any(test_table$skipped), !any(test_table$error),
          all(test_table$failed == 0L))
cat("Native prunlgp tests completed without failures, warnings or skips.\n")

The verified revision reports FAIL 0, WARN 0, SKIP 0, PASS 48 across 12 test cases. Counts may change as tests are added; zero failures, warnings and skips are the success criteria for the complete native run. Without DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_TESTS=true, only the lightweight tests execute and the Python tests are skipped: that is not a complete integration check.

Coverage includes output-specific input deletion, grouped model copies, information propagation, zero internal links, saved-model restoration, reproducibility, parallel candidates and invalid refits. This command tests the installed package; reinstall the fork after changing its source.

For a source-package check, first install the suggested check dependencies:

remotes::install_deps(dependencies=TRUE, upgrade="never")

Terminal:

R CMD build --no-manual .
R CMD check --no-manual --no-build-vignettes dgpsi_2.6.0-9000.tar.gz

Use the archive name printed by R CMD build if the package version changes. Check the final status and dgpsi.Rcheck/00check.log; the recorded check finished with Status: OK. A default package check does not execute Python tests or train the tutorials. Run the explicit native-test and tutorial commands above as separate checks.

7. Runtime and troubleshooting

On the recorded Windows 11 / R 4.4.2 / Python 3.10.20 setup, with Python already installed and numerical routines warmed up, the synthetic tutorial took about 60 seconds, the operational tutorial 81 seconds, and the native tests 148 seconds. Allow several minutes for each on a different machine. The first R/Python setup can take 10–30 minutes or longer, depending on downloads and dependency solving; this is a planning estimate, not a measured installation benchmark. First model runs can also take longer because Numba compiles numerical routines.

Symptom What to check
could not find function "prunlgp" Restart R, load dgpsi, inspect find.package("dgpsi") and the remote fields in section 2. Install the complete prunlgp-master branch rather than the CRAN package.
Rscript or R is not found in the terminal Add your R installation’s executable directory to PATH, or use the RStudio alternatives shown in this guide. Restart the terminal after changing PATH.
Dependency compilation fails Install the build tools matching your OS/R version and the system library named in the first build error. Then repeat the fork installation.
GitHub download fails or reaches an API limit Check network access to GitHub and retry. For authenticated downloads, configure a personal GitHub token through your local credential setup.
Downloads work in a browser but time out in R R may not inherit the system proxy. Configure R’s https_proxy and http_proxy environment variables for your network, and increase options(timeout=300) if needed.
Conda or Git cannot be found Run Sys.which("git") and reticulate::conda_binary() in R. Install the missing tool, restart R and perform section 3 interactively.
Python is already initialized from another environment Restart R before init_py(). Inspect Sys.getenv(c("RETICULATE_PYTHON", "RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV", "VIRTUAL_ENV")) for an unrelated override. Remove that override from this project’s configuration if you intend to use the managed environment.
A module is missing or the backend is inconsistent After initialization, inspect reticulate::py_config() and dgpsi.__file__ as above. Use the same explicit backend in examples, tests and workers.
Linux libstdc++.so.6, libcblas.so.3 or BLAS import error Follow the diagnostics from the master initializer and the upstream installation notes. Record the error and environment before rebuilding dependencies.
pandoc is unavailable Run rmarkdown::pandoc_available(). Use RStudio’s bundled Pandoc or install Pandoc. For a terminal session, ensure R can find it, for example through RSTUDIO_PANDOC pointing to the directory containing Pandoc.
HTML contains code but no fitted results Enable DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_VIGNETTE=true, or use the tutorial runner, which sets it for you.
Interactive networks disappear after copying HTML Keep the accompanying asset directories with non-self-contained HTML, or rerender in the destination directory.
Tests finish with SKIP Enable DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_TESTS=true and initialize Python. Skips do not establish that native prediction and pruning passed.
Results differ from the published table Compare R source commit, Python commit, seed, fitting settings and dependency versions. A moving dev backend is not a fixed software revision.

RETICULATE_PYTHON overrides other interpreter requests; see the reticulate environment documentation. Avoid loading a second Python environment in an already initialized R session.

For a reproducible problem report, include the first error, the command that caused it, and the output of:

sessionInfo()
packageDescription("dgpsi")[c("Version", "RemoteRef", "RemoteSha")]
reticulate::py_config()  # after initializing the intended environment

8. Versions and optional backend pinning

The recorded R baseline is upstream master commit ecd384343c53903517aa903ed7c8a150f4c5dc93. The current fork branch remains prunlgp-master; gh-pages holds the website. Numerical comparison records are in VALIDATION.md.

To use the recorded Python source rather than whichever revision dev later points to, first complete section 3 and close R. In a fresh R session, before loading dgpsi or initializing Python, install that source into the existing managed environment:

reticulate::conda_install(
  envname="dgp_si_R_2_6_0_dev",
  packages=paste0("git+https://github.com/mingdeyu/DGP.git@",
                  "480bb30260d3a1c22af1ddffe1a11df3e4de0820"),
  pip=TRUE, pip_options=c("--no-deps", "--force-reinstall")
)

This replaces the Python dgpsi source in that environment and keeps its installed dependencies. Restart R and use the same init_py(dgpsi_ver="dev") command without reinstall=TRUE. Pinning this source does not pin NumPy, SciPy or every other dependency; retain environment records when comparing results.

When updating the fork, reinstall it in a fresh R session, then rerun the tests and tutorials. The R and Python branches are versioned independently.

9. Sync with upstream

This is a formal fork of mingdeyu/dgpsi-R. The master branch is the recorded upstream baseline; prunlgp-master contains the extension and gh-pages the published website. Existing work is retained in a separate private backup.

From a clean clone of the extension branch, add the upstream remote once:

git remote add upstream https://github.com/mingdeyu/dgpsi-R.git
git fetch upstream
git switch prunlgp-master
git switch -c sync-upstream-master
git merge upstream/master

Resolve any conflicts, reinstall the package, and rerun section 6 and both tutorials before merging the update into prunlgp-master. Record the new upstream commit and any numerical changes in VALIDATION.md. Rebuild the website with tools/build-prunlgp-site.R; publish the checked docs/ contents to gh-pages. Updating the Python development backend is a separate change and should be validated separately.
